step_by_step_reasoning: The visual whiteboard architecture depicts a real-time call authentication and fraud detection pipeline. The pipeline starts with a customer (ThirdParty) sending SIP metadata to API Gateway. API Gateway triggers an authorization Lambda (top Lambda), which validates credentials against DynamoDB. Once authenticated, the request is passed to the main 'vera call' Lambda (bottom Lambda), which calls a SageMaker endpoint for spoofing/fraud risk prediction and returns a score back to the customer. Concurrently, the bottom Lambda asynchronously pushes the metadata to SQS, which then writes to S3 to allow SageMaker to periodically retrain the machine learning models. I have extracted all 8 nodes (including the external ThirdParty actor) and traced the arrows accurately according to the visual lines drawn on the board.

graph.name: NextCaller Phone Fraud Detection
graph.notes: Serverless architecture for real-time SIP metadata fraud detection and automatic machine learning model retraining.

nodes.name: Customer
nodes.notes: Sends real-time JSON-encoded SIP call metadata and receives a fraud risk score.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Ingests metadata requests and handles API routing.

nodes.name: Authorizer Lambda
nodes.notes: Custom authorizer that authenticates credentials using DynamoDB.

nodes.name: Vera Call Lambda
nodes.notes: The main product Lambda that evaluates the rules engine, requests predictions from SageMaker, and forwards metadata to SQS.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores customer credentials and API keys.

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: Hosts the prediction endpoint and manages model notebook/training jobs.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queues incoming metadata to decouple storage from real-time evaluation.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Encrypted S3 bucket storing customer metadata for training.
